to

From

Latent heat

2 · Investigate

Evaporation and water storage
Close investigation

Your question: When a puddle dries up, its water is gone forever.

Look for: Identify where liquid becomes vapor and where water can be stored. Explain why a drying puddle does not mean its water disappeared.

Model limit: The diagrams show possible transfers; they do not track a particular puddle or molecule.

Evaporation
Before
Liquid water
→
to
After
Water vapor
From
Ocean or surface water
To
Atmospheric vapor
Driver
Solar and surface thermal energy; wind transports vapor away
Latent heat
Latent heat absorbed

Water vapor is an invisible gas. Diagram marks represent its movement.

Collection
Before
Liquid or solid water
→
to
After
Stored liquid water or ice
From
Runoff, rivers, rain, or groundwater discharge
To
Surface water storage
Driver
Gravity routes water into surface stores
Latent heat
No latent heat transfer is required by this process.

Storage can last different lengths of time. Freezing and melting are separate possible processes.

myth.s: Water only evaporates when it is hot or boiling.
myth.why: Evaporation happens at every temperature — the fastest surface molecules escape even from cold water. Heat just speeds it up.

→
to

From

To

to

Evaporation and water storage
Close investigation

Your question: When a puddle dries up, its water is gone forever.

Model limit: The diagrams show possible transfers; they do not track a particular puddle or molecule.

Evaporation
Before
Liquid water
→
to
After
Water vapor
From
Ocean or surface water
To
Atmospheric vapor
Driver
Solar and surface thermal energy; wind transports vapor away
Latent heat
Latent heat absorbed

Water vapor is an invisible gas. Diagram marks represent its movement.

Collection
Before
Liquid or solid water
→
to
After
Stored liquid water or ice
From
Runoff, rivers, rain, or groundwater discharge
To
Surface water storage
Driver
Gravity routes water into surface stores
Latent heat
No latent heat transfer is required by this process.

Storage can last different lengths of time. Freezing and melting are separate possible processes.

myth.s: Clouds are made of water vapor.
myth.why: Clouds are liquid droplets (or ice crystals) condensed onto dust particles. Vapor is the invisible gas BEFORE condensation — if clouds were vapor, you could not see them.
myth.tryIt: Read the Condensation stage: vapor condenses onto tiny nuclei to become ~10 µm droplets.

quiz.q: What makes puddles disappear on sunny days?

wrongFeedback.Wind blows it away: Wind can help water evaporate faster by moving air, but the sun's heat is the main reason liquid water changes into gas.
wrongFeedback.It goes to sleep: Water molecules never sleep! The sun's energy makes them move faster and float up into the sky.

myth.s: Clouds are made of water vapor.
myth.why: Clouds are liquid droplets (or ice crystals) condensed onto dust particles. Vapor is the invisible gas BEFORE condensation — if clouds were vapor, you could not see them.
